canonical_unit_note: ₹/piece. Also quoted per 1,000 and, for AAC, per cubic metre — a ₹/piece band and a ₹/cum band differ by roughly the number of blocks in a cubic metre, so the conversion needs piece volume from the size attribute.
counts_note: Counts measured from data/buildobjects.db on 2026-08-17 for hyderabad. Each count is a number of OFFERS, not products: the results list shows one card per vendor, so the rail counts sellers' listings and these numbers match it exactly. A facet marked data_backed:false has no field behind it in the collected data and ships disabled with a reason.
lead_reason: These are entirely different products with different masonry practice, different mortar and different wall thickness — not variants of one thing. Nothing else on the panel is decidable until it is chosen.

filters.label: Type
filters.why: The defining decision and the parent of the size ladder — clay, AAC and concrete blocks have completely different size vocabularies, so one flat Size filter would be meaningless.

filters.label: Size
filters.why: AAC runs a 600×200 face with the thickness as the variable — the thickness is the wall decision (100 mm partition, 200 mm external).

filters.label: Size
filters.why: The Indian standard modular brick is 230×110×75 mm; the traditional country brick varies by kiln and is sold as a separate value rather than pretending to a standard it does not meet.

filters.label: Size
filters.why: Concrete blocks run a 400×200 face with thickness as the variable, the same shape of decision as AAC but a different ladder.
filters.no_data_reason: No collected listing in hyderabad populates `attrs.size_mm`. The facet is retained and shipped disabled rather than deleted, so the gap is visible rather than silently absent.

filters.label: Compressive strength
filters.why: The load-bearing decision. A 3.5 N/mm² block in a load-bearing wall is a structural failure, not a saving — so this is a safety filter and never folded.
filters.no_data_reason: No collected listing in hyderabad populates `attrs.compressive_strength_nmm2`. The facet is retained and shipped disabled rather than deleted, so the gap is visible rather than silently absent.

filters.label: Brand
filters.why: Branded supply is real in AAC and almost absent in clay brick, where the market is local kilns. 'Local / unbranded' is a first-class value here, not a fallback — it is most of the honest supply.

filters.label: Order quantity
filters.why: Masonry is bought by the lorry load, and the per-piece rate moves sharply with it. Most sellers here quote a minimum in thousands, so this facet also prevents a cart that cannot be fulfilled.
filters.no_data_reason: No collected listing in hyderabad populates `offer.bulk_slabs`. The facet is retained and shipped disabled rather than deleted, so the gap is visible rather than silently absent.

filters.label: BIS mark
filters.why: Labels, never hides — and this is the category where that matters most. Local clay bricks from a Krishna-district kiln are legal, ordinary, widely used material carrying no BIS mark. A default-on certification filter would delete most of the real supply and substitute our judgement for the buyer's.
filters.note: Default off. 'Not applicable' is the honest state for most local kiln supply, and it is neutral — not a failure.

values.label: Not applicable
values.sublabel: no standard applies to this product

filters.label: Arrives
filters.why: Computed per pincode from the freight model. Masonry is the most freight-sensitive category in the set — a kiln 60 km out can be cheaper ex-yard and dearer delivered.

filters.label: Fly ash content
filters.why: This attribute decides the tax rate, not just the recipe: AAC with fly ash over 50% falls under HSN 6815 at 12%, below that under 6810 at 18%. A six-point GST difference on the same-looking block is exactly the kind of hidden basis error this engine exists to surface.
filters.needs_verification: The >50% fly-ash threshold comes from the 55th GST Council clarification as recorded in the spec's Appendix C. Confirm against the notification text before this drives an invoice.

values.label: Not published by seller
values.sublabel: rate shown at the higher slab

filters.no_data_reason: No collected listing in hyderabad populates `attrs.fly_ash_pct`. The facet is retained and shipped disabled rather than deleted, so the gap is visible rather than silently absent.

filters.label: Finish
filters.why: Wire-cut bricks have square arrises and take exposed brickwork; table-moulded do not. Only meaningful for clay.
filters.no_data_reason: No collected listing in hyderabad populates `attrs.finish`. The facet is retained and shipped disabled rather than deleted, so the gap is visible rather than silently absent.

filters.label: Density
filters.why: AAC's whole selling point is dead-load reduction — a 550 kg/m³ block against a 1,900 kg/m³ clay brick changes the structural design. Folded because it is largely implied by Type.

filters.label: IS standard
filters.why: Specifying engineers work from the IS code. Folded because it maps one-to-one onto Type.

filters.label: Seller quotes price
filters.why: Clay bricks are 12% with ITC or 6% without — the 5% figure repeated across the web died on 2022-04-01 and would systematically under-price every BOQ built on it.

filters.label: Price verified
filters.why: Bricks and blocks are volatility class V0 — a 24 h SLA, because they are freight-dominated and diesel-linked.
filters.no_data_reason: No collected listing in hyderabad populates `price_current.freshness_state`. The facet is retained and shipped disabled rather than deleted, so the gap is visible rather than silently absent.
